Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
301 AM EDT Mon Oct 19 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 300 AM EDT Monday...

No significant changes to the current forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 300 AM EDT Monday...

1. Quiet and dry weather is expected through the late week.

2. The extended forecast continues to be very quiet with 
seasonable temperatures and dry conditions prevail through next 
weekend. 
  

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 300 AM EDT Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: High pressure 1037 mb is currently centered over Nova 
Scotia early this morning as a low level jet blows across Ontario 
and Quebec. This is resulting in clear skies and breezy conditions 
on mountaintops. Temperatures this morning in the 30s and 40s will 
rebound into the lower 60s by the afternoon hours under southerly 
flow. A weak moisture starved cold front will slide south from 
Canada Monday night into Tuesday and wash out over the area with no 
precipitation expected, though some morning clouds and cooler 
temperatures can be expected Tuesday morning. Sunny skies will 
prevail thereafter with large scale ridging leading to low humidity 
and light winds through mid week. There continues to be high 
confidence of no precipitation areawide at least through mid week.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Little change in the forecast provided by WPC this 
package with temps trending cooler than normal by late week and dry 
conditions prevailing. A weak cold front will drop south late Thurs 
into Friday with northerly winds and cooler 925mb to 850mb thermal 
profiles. The latest ECMWF is most aggressive with showing a closing 
700 to 500mb circulation and the potential for a few 
sprinkles/flurries, while the GFS/CMC are less robust with trof 
development and associated caa. The probability of measurable precip 
is <10% attm, so have no mention of pops in latest fcst. Based on 
progged 850mb temps btwn 0C and -2C and similar 925mb temps, the 
highs provided by WPC are in the upper 30s mtns summits to l/m 50s 
valleys on Friday and warm into the mid 40s to upper 50s by Saturday 
and mostly mid 50s to lower 60s by Sunday. Lows generally in the mid 
20s to mid 30s, warming back into the mid 30s to lower 40s by 
Sunday. As daily nocturnal inversion develop by next weekend, expect 
a sharp thermal gradient between cooler/sheltered valleys and warmer 
midslope/ridges to persist. These temperature details are not very 
well captured by the latest forecast provided by WPC. 

Fire weather concerns increase this week, given the dry conditions, 
mild temperatures and sunshine, significant drying of fine fuels, 
including leaf litter is expected, but winds are expected to remain 
light.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Through 06Z Tuesday...Primary aviation hazard will be localized
wind shear at MSS through 10z this morning associated with 2000
feet above ground jet of 35 to 40 knots. Otherwise, high
confidence of VFR conditions prevailing the next 24 hours at all
TAF sites, with south to southwest winds 5 to 15 knots.
